accepted_classes: Per brief; VRT P1-P4 classes with demonstrated impact
bugcrowd.consequences: Points by VRT priority (P1=40 down to P5=0); accuracy affects invites
bugcrowd.dedupe: First fully reproducible report awarded; same-codebase instances of one issue are duplicates
out_of_scope: Targets not listed in the brief
bugcrowd.scope: Program brief plus VRT severity baseline; only listed targets

accepted_classes: Per program policy and severity table
hackerone.consequences: Reputation: +7 triaged/resolved, -5 Not Applicable, -10 Spam; low Signal restricts report volume
out_of_scope: Scanner-only output without a demonstrated vulnerability
hackerone.scope: Program policy page overrides all defaults; only listed assets

intigriti.consequences: Reputation from accepted reports by severity; validity ratio drives visibility and private invites
intigriti.scope: Program scope page; identity check required for payouts

open_bug_bounty.consequences: No platform bounties; recognition through coordinated disclosure
open_bug_bounty.dedupe: Signed-in dedupe re-check immediately before filing is mandatory
out_of_scope: Anything requiring authentication bypass attempts against third parties
open_bug_bounty.scope: Non-intrusive testing only (XSS/CSRF class), ISO 29147 coordinated disclosure

accepted_classes: Arbitrary file upload/deletion with full path+extension control
Broken access control / IDOR with significant impact
patchstack.attacker_privilege: Unauthenticated or Subscriber/Customer (Contributor+ only via mVDP-covered components)
patchstack.consequences: Rejection rate >=50% removes the researcher from the monthly leaderboard for one month plus cooldown; rule-violating or untested reports can draw a one-week ban; monthly bounty is reduced by rejection rate
patchstack.dedupe: First valid report wins, even across different endpoints of the same root cause
out_of_scope: Blind SSRF and most race conditions (rule 4.10)
Payment bypass (rule 3.9, not an accepted type)
Minor record changes without significant impact (rule 3.9)
patchstack.scope: WordPress plugins/themes, >=1000 installs, latest version, updated within 3 years

accepted_classes: High Threat classes (RCE, arbitrary file upload, SQLi, stored XSS, privilege escalation, authentication bypass)
wordfence.consequences: Tiered bounties plus monthly streak bonuses; rejected classes earn nothing
out_of_scope: Issues requiring Contributor/Author or high privileges
wordfence.scope: WordPress plugins/themes with install-tier gates (High Threat >=25 installs; stored XSS/SQLi >=500; Standard tier >=50k for other classes)

yeswehack.consequences: Points and credits from accepted reports; no disclosure without program permission
yeswehack.dedupe: One fix, one reward: first reporter of the root cause wins
out_of_scope: Missing security headers or cookie flags alone
yeswehack.scope: Program scope page; report promptly through the platform only

pre_submission_checklist: Asset and program scope match confirmed on the live scope page
Vulnerability class is on the platform's accepted list, with its conditions met
Exclusion list checked (out-of-scope classes, severity caps, privilege limits)
Attacker privilege is within the platform limit (unauthenticated or lowest accepted role)
Attack complexity is low; no prerequisite tricks the platform rejects
Impact is significant and demonstrated, not theoretical
Target version is current and install/eligibility thresholds are met
Dedupe checked twice: platform search and vendor changelog/patch diff
One root cause per report; related instances grouped, not split
PoC replays end-to-end from the report alone
CVSS is honest and within the program cap for the class
Rolling rejection + duplicate rate checked; pause and re-triage if it climbs
target: Keep rejection + duplicate rate below 2% across all platforms. Run the pre-submission checklist before every filing; a finding that fails scope, accepted-class, or dedupe checks is routed to vendor disclosure instead of a platform submission.
